what_it_is: Runtime authorization platform for humans, non-human identities and AI agents, MCP tools and RAG.
identity_note: PlainID Policy Manager and the Agentic Identity Platform. In October 2026 PlainID relaunched its brand as the Runtime Authorization Platform for the AI era.

1.reason: Discovers agents, MCP servers, tools and vector stores for authorization. No shadow AI scan or AI cloud posture.
1.evidence: Agent, tool, MCP, and resource discovery
1.has: Platform Discover pillar finds agents, MCP tools, resources. AgentCore and Foundry agent discovery.
1.lacks: No AI cloud resource inventory. No endpoint shadow AI scan. No CI/CD checks.

2.reason: MCP guardrail discovers MCP tools and enforces tool and parameter policy. Supports AWS AgentCore and Microsoft Foundry.
2.evidence: govern which tools are visible, whether they can be invoked, which operations can be performed, and which parameter values
2.has: MCP Guardrail, native MCP Gateway, AI-Ready Gateway Enforcement, AgentCore and Foundry support.
2.lacks: No agent sandbox. Two named managed platforms. Authorization only, no host isolation.

3.reason: Authorization decisions deny tool calls and prompts at runtime. Telemetry goes to SIEM. No attack detection.
3.evidence: Authorization telemetry can also be shared with enterprise SIEM and security analytics systems.
3.has: Runtime deny of prompts and tool calls. Authorization telemetry to SIEM. Zero standing privileges.
3.lacks: No attack or anomaly detection. No named SIEM or ITSM. No host-level blocking.

4.reason: Four guardrails control input, retrieval, MCP tools and output with masking. No injection or jailbreak detection.
4.evidence: Interprets user intent, reads identity signals, evaluates policy permissions, and approves or blocks prompts in real time.
4.has: Input and output guardrails. Gateway, framework and Kong, Apigee, Envoy enforcement.
4.lacks: No injection or jailbreak detection. No toxicity or hallucination filters. No browser extension.

5.reason: Decision logs record agent, user, policy and outcome for audits. Blogs map to EU AI Act and OWASP.
5.evidence: PlainID records the identity, resource, action, evaluated context, applicable policy, and decision outcome.
5.has: Authorization audit and insights. Policy360 graph of agents, tools and data.
5.lacks: No AIBOM export. No in-product framework mapping or report export found.

6.reason: No red teaming or attack library found. PlainID enforces authorization and does not test models.
6.evidence: Searched: PlainID red teaming, adversarial testing AI agents, jailbreak testing. No PlainID page or product found.
6.lacks: No attack library, no multi-turn attacks, no CI/CD red teaming.

7.reason: Authorizes each agent request on agent plus user identity, per tool and parameter, with zero standing privileges.
7.evidence: Human, NHI, and Agent Identity are all considered in the enforcement flow.
7.has: Per-tool and parameter policy, composite user-agent identity, just-in-time access, agent registry.
7.lacks: No own agent credential. No API key or secret vaulting or rotation.

8.reason: Filters RAG retrieval and masks responses by policy. No dataset, model or code scanning.
8.evidence: restrict which data and documents AI can retrieve to generate insights from Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems
8.has: Data Retrieval Guardrail filters RAG and vector store access by policy.
8.lacks: No PII or poisoning scans of datasets. No model scanning. No AI SAST.

notes: PlainID is an authorization vendor, so most AI security modules are enforcement or nothing. It is not acquired. SAP has made a strategic investment (undisclosed amount). Gartner named it a Representative Vendor in the 2026 Market Guide for Guardian Agents. The Agentic Identity Platform was announced as a pre-release and early access in 2026, so the guardrail and discovery claims in modules 1, 2, 4 and 7 may be early. AI-Ready Gateway Enforcement was announced October 6, 2026 and is new. Agent platform support named on the site is AWS AgentCore and Microsoft Foundry (May 2026), plus LangChain, LangGraph and OpenClaw plugins. Gateway integrations include Kong, Apigee, Envoy and AWS API Gateway. PlainID blogs state it layers on top of NHI inventory, vaulting and rotation tools, so 7.3 is partial. 8.2 is partial only because retrieval is governed by policy. PlainID does not scan datasets. 3.1 is no because no detection product was found. PlainID compares itself with Zenity and notes Zenity covers posture while PlainID enforces.
